clue.text: Conductor grabs novice, originator of musical confusion

indicators.note: the conductor word holds the novice letter inside it, as if grabbing it

parts.note: a maestro is a great conductor of an orchestra
L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver

indicators.note: the originator of a word is its opening letter, here of musical

explanation.surface: An orchestra's conductor takes hold of a beginner, which sets off chaos in the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively any turbulent state of turmoil.

clue.text: A disease mother's keeping quiet

indicators.note: the mother's word keeps the quiet letter held within it

parts.note: mum is mother, and the possessive keeps its S
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: An illness strikes while a mother keeps silent about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a contagious viral illness that swells the glands of the neck.

clue.text: Caught on the street dividing soft drug

indicators.note: the caught and street letters split the soft word into two parts

parts.note: easy means soft, as in a soft option
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested on the street handing out a soft drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name of the stimulant MDMA, an illegal recreational drug.

clue.text: With holidays coming up green somehow becomes cleaner

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the holidays word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: vacs is short for vacations, i.e. holidays

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of green are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: After the holidays a green character somehow turns into a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns VACS into SCAV; 'somehow' rearranges GREEN as ENGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger feeds on refuse and carrion, so it clears away waste like a street sweeper.

clue.text: Inclined to make less use of sinister member

definitions.text: Inclined to make less use of sinister member

parts.words: Inclined to make less use of sinister member
parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, so the member used less is the left hand; a person inclined that way favours the other one

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mainly uses the dexter hand naturally uses the left one less.

clue.text: This plan upsets lady

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsets means the lady's name is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Pam is a woman's name, a lady

explanation.surface: A lady takes offence at this scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A map is a plan or chart of an area.

clue.text: Loopy pattern on bed is very good

indicators.note: on places the very good word up against the bed word, which follows it

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword slang for very good
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A looped design on the bed looks very fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop of thread forming an edging on lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Source of hay fever?

explanation.surface: A question about what triggers hay fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is a grass grown for fodder, and a panic is a frantic agitated state, a fever of fear.

clue.text: Cry about game? Don't be so gloomy!

parts.note: a cheer is a shout or cry of encouragement
being game means being willing, as in up for it

explanation.surface: Someone moaning about a match is told to stop sulking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link: a cry about being game. Game means willing, the same as up in 'up for anything'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheer up is the imperative telling someone to stop being miserable.

clue.text: See arts given new look, including city museum items?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters include the city within them
the letters of see and arts are refashioned into a new arrangement

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Viewers see artworks redisplayed in a city museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given new look' rearranges SEEARTS as TREASES; 'including' puts UR inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasures are precious objects, the kind of valuables a museum displays.

clue.text: Essential requirement: wild nag

parts.note: a must is something essential, a requirement

indicators.note: wild says the letters of nag run wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something indispensable is an untamed horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges NAG as ANG; it also colours the definition, since the horse is a wild one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a feral horse of the American plains, and nag is slang for a horse.

clue.text: Beastly fever? Yearn to comprehend explanation

indicators.note: comprehend in its old sense of contain, so the yearn word holds the explanation word

parts.note: to pine is to yearn or long
a key is an explanation, as for a map or code

explanation.surface: Someone longs to understand the reason for an animal's illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinkeye is a contagious fever of horses as well as an eye inflammation in livestock, so a disease of beasts.

clue.text: Lodgings in Kent, say, for one in suit?

indicators.note: the lodgings word sits inside the south-east letters

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England, so SE for South East
a pad is slang for one's lodgings or flat

explanation.surface: Someone renting rooms in Kent asks whether to wear a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is a suit of playing cards, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade is a card of one of the four suits in a pack.

clue.text: Star medic going wobbly? Show how many hours are worked!

definitions.text: Show how many hours are worked

indicators.note: going wobbly suggests the letters of star medic losing their order

explanation.surface: A celebrity doctor loses composure and is told to prove the hours put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Time cards are records stamped by a clock that display the hours an employee has worked.

clue.text: Girl getting the job to fail as a secretary?

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl
taken as written
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A young woman lands the position and then flops as a secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss the post is to fail to send letters before collection, a secretary's failing.

clue.text: Laurel is graduate with Third in Psychology

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: the third letter in the word Psychology is taken

explanation.surface: A man named Laurel graduated with a third-class degree in psychology.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a third-class degree; here it is just the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay is another name for the laurel tree, whose leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Cover of darkness?

parts.note: taken literally, a covering used when it is dark, at night in bed, rather than the idiom for concealment

explanation.definitionFit: A bedspread is a decorative top cover laid over a bed, which is used at night.

clue.text: Jumper in rags put off possible purchaser

indicators.note: put off suggests the letters of rags being put out of order

parts.note: a shopper is someone who may buy

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a jumper and rags puts off a would-be buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater; it is the leaping insect. 'put off' rearranges RAGS as GRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasshopper is an insect that leaps on long hind legs.

clue.text: Chipping a painting?

parts.note: a painting that is chipping must be aged, a great old work by a pre-modern artist

explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a work by a great European painter before about 1800, old enough for its paint to flake.

clue.text: Record getting amended after first in race is disgraced

indicators.note: after places the amended word following the first letter of race

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: first in takes the opening letter of race

parts.note: edited means amended

explanation.surface: A record result revised after the leader of the race is shamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Discredited means having lost reputation, brought into disrepute.

clue.text: Older folk making horrible snores about an hour after midnight

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the hour letter
horrible suggests the letters of snores in a dreadful mess

parts.note: one o'clock, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Elderly people snore dreadfully at about one in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges SNORES as SENORS; 'about' puts I (one o'clock) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniors are elderly people, senior citizens.

clue.text: Vehicle is broken having lost tailpiece

indicators.note: the final letter of the broken word is lost, its tail cut off

parts.note: bust means broken

explanation.surface: A car is broken down after losing its rear section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost tailpiece' drops the T from BUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Animal has dull yellow thing shining round ead

parts.note: buff is a pale dull yellow colour

indicators.note: written as a Cockney would say head, the H is dropped from the shining ring word

parts.note: a halo is a ring of light shining around a saint's head

explanation.surface: A beast has a dull yellow ring shining round its head.
explanation.walkthrough: ''ead' is head with its H dropped in Cockney fashion, so the H of HALO goes, leaving ALO.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffalo is a large wild ox, such as the Asian water buffalo or the American bison.

clue.text: Sleep around and manage to beg in the street

indicators.note: around turns the sleep word back to front

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
to handle something is to manage it

explanation.surface: A vagrant sleeps around and manages to scrounge in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: PANHANDLE is US slang, from holding out a hand like a pan for coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To panhandle is US slang for begging from passers-by.

clue.text: Old skeleton, a man, end of century

parts.note: Tom is a man's name

indicators.note: the end of century is its final letter

explanation.surface: An old skeleton turns out to be a man from the end of the century.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomy is an archaic word for a skeleton or emaciated body, a corruption of anatomy.

clue.text: Unpleasant hag, wife — ugly, odd bits missing!

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of hag, wife, ugly are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A rude remark calls a wife an ugly hag, with bits left unsaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad or disagreeable.

clue.text: Lord's province in Belgium

explanation.surface: A nobleman owns a region of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal superior owed allegiance; Liege is also a French-speaking province of eastern Belgium.

clue.text: Environmental science record held by English company

indicators.note: the record word is held inside the English and company letters

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for company
a log is a record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: An environmental study is recorded and kept by an English firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecology is the study of how organisms relate to each other and their surroundings.

clue.text: Sheep's heard in this wood

indicators.note: heard says the sheep word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Sheep can be heard bleating among these trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Yew is the tough, springy timber of the yew tree, used for longbows.

clue.text: It's improper pocketing silver — an immoral act

indicators.note: the improper word pockets the silver symbol inside it

parts.note: outre means beyond what is proper, unconventional
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: It's wrong to pocket silver, a wicked deed.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shockingly wicked or offensive deed.

clue.text: Attractive little girl not inclined to communicate

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
shy means reserved, reluctant to talk

explanation.surface: A pretty young girl is reluctant to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British for good-looking.

clue.text: Where a lot may get drunk?

definitions.text: Where a lot may get drunk?

parts.words: Where a lot may get drunk?
parts.note: reads like a rowdy bar, but means a place where much liquid is drunk, by thirsty animals

explanation.definitionFit: A waterhole is a pool where wild animals gather to drink.
